'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
***The [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition launches [[airstrike]]s on [[Sanaa International Airport]] in the [[Yemen]]i capital [[Sanaa]]. The air raid targeted six sites, including places used for "launching [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] attacks", according to a statement from the coalition. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-led-coalition-asks-civilians-immediately-evacuate-sanaa-airport-al-arabiya-2021-12-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**The [[French Army]] announces that they have killed Soumana Boura, a leading member of the [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara]], the previous day. Boura was involved in the [[Kouré shooting|killings of six]] [[French people|French]] [[Humanitarian aid|aid workers]] and their two Nigerien guides in a [[mass shooting]] in August 2020 in [[Kouré, Niger|Kouré]], [[Niger]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/12/21/france-says-killed-suspect-in-2020-murder-of-aid-workers-in-niger (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[Tigray Defense Forces]] withdraws all its troops from the [[Afar Region|Afar]] and [[Amhara Region|Amhara]] [[regions of Ethiopia]]. [https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2021/12/21/ethiopia-tigrayan-forces-quit-afar-amhara/ (PM News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[December 2021 Malaysian floods]]
**Heavy [[flood]]s continue to affect eight [[Malaysia]]n [[states of Malaysia|states]] for the third day, killing 14 people and partially submerging several towns and villages. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-59723341 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany]]
*****The [[Standing Committee on Vaccination]] recommends the shortening of the interval between the second dose and [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to three months and urges all citizens over the age of 18 to receive a booster dose of an mRNA-based vaccine after receiving their first two doses in order to reduce the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-recommends-covid-19-boosters-after-3-months/ (''Politico.eu'')]
****[[Germany|German]] [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Olaf Scholz]] and 16 [[States of Germany|state]] premiers agree to tighten the restrictions beginning on December 28, including limiting the number of people in private gatherings to 10 and banning spectators at large-scale musical, sporting and cultural events due to concerns related to the spread of the Omicron variant. [https://www.dw.com/en/omicron-germany-to-limit-private-gatherings-after-christmas/a-60206476 (Deutsche Welle)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Community of Madrid]]
*****The [[Community of Madrid]] reports a record 11,221 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.abc.es/espana/madrid/abci-record-contagios-covid-madrid-11221-casos-9518-ultimas-24-horas-y-6-fallecidos-202112211847_noticia.html (ABC.es)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Prime Minister of Portugal|Prime Minister]] [[António Costa]] announces that nightclubs and bars will be closed and all people will work from home for at least two weeks beginning on December 25 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. There will also be capacity restrictions at shops and people will require a negative [[COVID-19 test]] in order to enter events. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-12-21/portugal-s-nightclubs-bars-to-close-a-week-earlier-than-planned (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****The [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[Government of Sweden|government]] announces that several new measures will begin on December 23, including limiting the number of people at private gatherings to 50, requiring the use of a vaccination pass for public events with a capacity of more than 500 people, and recommending [[work from home]] where possible, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/sweden-tightens-covid-restrictions-cases-mount-2021-12-21/ (Reuters)]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Commission]] announces a binding proposal that will make the [[Vaccine passports during the COVID-19 pandemic#Europe#European Union|EU Digital COVID Certificate]] only valid for travel within the [[European Union]] for nine months without a [[booster dose]] after a person's primary vaccination schedule in order to standardize different travel requirements in the member states. The new rules will be mandatory for all 27 EU member states beginning on February 1. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/europe/20211221-eu-sets-a-mandatory-9-month-validity-of-vaccinations-for-covid-19-travel-pass (RFI)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
*****The [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Health ministry]] recommends that [[Israelis]] over the age of 60 years and healthcare workers should receive a fourth dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, becoming the world's first country to administer a fourth dose of the vaccine. The move is welcomed by [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-israel-to-offer-fourth-vaccine-dose-to-over-60s-saying-it-is-first-nation-to-roll-it-out-12501771 (Sky News)]
****[[Israel]] reports its first confirmed death related to the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] in a man in his 60s with pre-existing health conditions who died at the [[Soroka Medical Center]] in [[Beersheba]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israel-reportedly-records-first-known-omicron-death/ (''The Times of Israel'')] The hospital later states that the death was actually because of the Delta variant. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/hospital-reverses-course-says-covid-linked-death-was-delta-not-omicron/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] reduces the interval of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] [[booster dose]] to three months for people who received a two-dose vaccine and two months for people who received a single-dose vaccine in order to reduce the effects of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]]s. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/815478/fda-approves-shortening-of-interval-for-covid-19-booster-shots-duque/story/ (GMA News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reinstates its mandatory hotel [[quarantine]] for all incoming foreign travellers and suspends the "sandbox" program for places other than [[Phuket]] after the country reported its first locally transmitted case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]. [https://www.rappler.com/world/asia-pacific/thailand-reinstates-mandatory-covid-19-quarantine-omicron-concerns/ (Rappler)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Argentina]]
****The provinces of [[Buenos Aires Province|Buenos Aires]], [[Córdoba Province (Argentina)|Córdoba]], [[Santa Fe Province|Santa Fe]], [[Río Negro Province|Río Negro]] and [[Santiago del Estero Province|Santiago del Estero]] begin implementing the usage of a "sanitary pass" for large events. [https://www.pagina12.com.ar/390753-en-que-provincias-comenzo-a-ser-obligatorio-el-pase-sanitari (''Página/12'')]
***[[Argentina]] reports 9,336 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the highest daily total in 4 months, thereby bringing the nationwide total of cases to 5.4 million. [https://www.iprofesional.com/actualidad/354234-coronavirus-9-336-casos-nuevos-la-cifra-mas-alta-en-4-meses (IProfesional)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] postpones a phased reopening of the border for quarantine-free travel to the end of February in order to strengthen the country's defence against the spread of the Omicron variant. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/dec/21/new-zealand-delays-border-reopening-in-bid-to-strengthen-defences-against-omicron (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] announces that healthcare workers will be required to receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster dose in order to keep their "fully vaccinated" status, becoming the second state to impose such mandate. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/california-becomes-second-state-require-healthcare-workers-get-booster-shots-n1286421 (NBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Lithuania–United States relations]], [[Second Cold War]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] approves the sale of 341 [[FGM-148 Javelin]] [[anti-tank guided missile]]s and 30 command launch units to [[NATO]] ally [[Lithuania]] amid rising tensions with [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/us-approves-sale-javelin-missiles-lithuania-russia-tensions-build-2021-12-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Japan]]
**Three inmates in Japan are [[Capital punishment|executed]] by [[hanging]], marking the first executions in the country in nearly two years. One inmate was the perpetrator of a 2004 [[mass stabbing]] in which he killed seven of his relatives. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/12/21/us-japan-executions (Euronews)]
